Pro V2 is the engine behind every measurement — a detection core that holds steady between runs and measures amplitude (°) — the balance wheel’s swing (healthy watches typically read 220–300°). It also shows the averaged tick/tock waveform under the chart; sharp spikes mean a clean signal. Amplitude appears only when the signal is clean enough to trust. Measuring twice and comparing is the quickest way to know a reading is trustworthy.

Tap the ⚙ gear (top-right of the Measure screen) to adjust how the engine listens: a Precision preset — Quick (~10s), Balanced (~17s, recommended) or Strict (~33s, tightest) — and the movement’s lift angle (52° fits most modern movements). Longer presets listen to more of the watch before answering, so readings repeat more closely; the quickest rescue for a watch that won’t converge is Strict plus a quieter room and the watch resting directly on the microphone edge.

Tap the bell in the top-right corner to see likes, comments, and follow requests. Tapping a like or comment notification opens the Feed. Tapping a follow request notification lets you accept or decline.

Tap the heart to like any post. Tap the comment bubble to read and leave comments. To remove a comment, tap the ⋮ menu on it — you can delete your own comments anywhere, and any comment on your own posts. You'll get a bell notification when someone likes or comments on your posts.
Tap the streak counter to open a month calendar of every day you logged, with your current and best streak.

Tap the three-dot menu on a post and select Block User, or go to their profile and choose Block User from the three-dot menu. Blocked users won’t appear in your feed and cannot interact with your content. You can manage your block list from your profile page.

Tap the view icon at the top to cycle list → brand folders → gallery → compact — like the Collection toggle, the icon shows the view you'll get next. The folder view groups watches from the same brand into collapsible folders — every brand gets one, even if you only have a single watch from it — handy when several grails share a maker. The gallery view shows a photo-first grid, and compact shrinks it to tiny tiles so the whole wishlist fits on one screen.
Tap your avatar in the top-right to open your profile, then tap the edit icon to edit your display name, @username, bio, and profile photo.

The Collection Value tile totals the market values you have saved (nothing is refreshed behind your back) against what you paid, and says when they were last checked and how many are older than 60 days or missing. Tap the tile to run Update prices for the whole collection.

The app now speaks Spanish, Italian, French, Turkish, German and Portuguese as well as English. Open your profile and pick one under Language — menus, buttons, dates and the Help guide switch over, and so do the emails, notifications and fun facts we send you. Your choice follows your account to every device. Spot a translation that reads wrong? Tell us through Send Feedback.

The chips above the grid sort by Newest (purchase date), Most Worn, Last Worn (freshest on the wrist first, never-worn last, with a “how long ago” note on each card) and, once you’ve played the Ranking Game, My Ranking. For price, market value and cost-per-wear sorting, tap the report icon next to Share to open the sortable table in Stats.
The database is still growing, so some models may be missing or incomplete. They’re added as members add watches to their collections.

The date defaults to today. Tap Yesterday or Pick date to log retroactively. The Today's Pick card suggests a watch based on your rotation — tap Log This Wear to log it directly. Didn't wear anything? Tap Didn't wear a watch today under the watch list — the day is recorded as deliberately watch-free, keeps your streak going, and never touches your wear stats.

The flame counter in the top bar shows how many days in a row you’ve logged a wear — any log counts. It dims when today isn’t logged yet, so log something to keep it lit.

The full app — timegrapher, collection, wear tracking and the social feed — is now on Google Play. Search for WRotate or grab it from the badge on wrotate.com; sign in with the same account and everything syncs across your devices.

The month-in-review card can now spot a habit in your wear log and give it a slide of its own: the watch that owned your Saturdays, a comeback after months in the box, a run of days back to back on one watch, or the watch you most often reach for next. One pattern per month, and only when the numbers genuinely back it up — no slide beats a stretched claim.

The view name at the top left of the Feed (All posts) is a menu: switch to People I follow, Close friends or My posts. It also names the view when you open one member’s posts from their profile or one model’s posts from its page — pick All posts there to go back to the full feed.

The watch database now has its own Watches tab in the main menu. Your Wishlist moved in with your collection: open the Collection tab and switch between Collection and Wishlist at the top. Everything on it — views, ranking, AI picks, share links — works exactly as before.
